name: Mishra Dhatu Nigam Limited (MIDHANI)

header.one_liner: India's strategic special-metals PSU under the Ministry of Defence; sole domestic source of many superalloys, titanium alloys, maraging and armour steels for aero-engines, missiles, launch vehicles and warships. FY26 turnover ₹1,208.63 crore (+12.5% YoY), order book ₹2,290 crore.
header.indigenous_label: Import-substitution metals producer; melts and processes superalloys, titanium and special steels domestically, but depends on imported sponge titanium, nickel, cobalt and certain master alloys

at_a_glance.Ownership: Public Sector Undertaking (Mini Ratna) under the Ministry of Defence, Government of India
at_a_glance.Product_families: Superalloys, titanium alloys, special/maraging steels, armour-grade steel, investment castings, forgings, fasteners, welding consumables

what_it_is.prose: Mishra Dhatu Nigam Limited (MIDHANI) is a Mini Ratna Public Sector Undertaking under the Ministry of Defence, Government of India, headquartered at Kanchanbagh, Hyderabad, and incorporated in 1973 to make India self-reliant in strategic metallurgical materials that were denied under Cold War technology-control regimes. MIDHANI melts, forges, rolls and casts superalloys, titanium alloys, special and maraging steels, armour-grade steels, investment castings, forgings, fasteners and welding consumables for the aerospace, defence, space, atomic-energy and energy sectors. It is the principal — and in many grades the sole — domestic source of high-temperature nickel-cobalt superalloys and titanium alloys used in aero gas-turbine engines, missile motor cases (maraging steel for Agni-class strategic missiles), launch-vehicle hardware for ISRO (including materials associated with the LVM-3 and Chandrayaan programmes), and naval and armour applications. Customers include DRDO, ISRO, HAL, the Indian armed forces, BrahMos Aerospace and the Department of Atomic Energy. For FY26 MIDHANI reported record revenue from operations of ₹1,208.63 crore (up 12.52% year-on-year), Profit After Tax of ₹130.79 crore (up 18.82%), a Q4 FY26 revenue of ₹552.75 crore (up 34.63%), and a closing order book of ₹2,290 crore as of 1 April 2026, alongside record titanium-alloy production of about 700 tonnes. On 13 August 2026 MIDHANI became the first Indian company to secure GE Aerospace S400 laboratory approval for chemical, mechanical and metallurgical testing of metallic materials to GE Aerospace standards — a qualification that positions it inside global aero-engine supply chains. In February 2025 it signed an MoU with the Aeronautical Development Agency for indigenous development of high-strength, high-toughness special steel for combat-aircraft programmes (Tejas Mk-2, AMCA, TEDBF).

deployments_procurement.summary: MIDHANI is not a platform builder but a materials backbone: its output is embedded in Indian aero-engines, strategic and tactical missiles, launch vehicles, warships and armour. FY26 was a record year with turnover of ₹1,208.63 crore and an order book of ₹2,290 crore. Strategic milestones in the review period include the February 2025 ADA MoU on combat-aircraft special steel, development of cast single-crystal superalloy blade material for aero engines, NADCAP certification of a new aerospace fasteners facility, and the August 2026 GE Aerospace S400 lab approval (first in India).

import_dependencies.summary: MIDHANI is itself India's import-substitution answer for finished strategic metals, but its upstream raw-material and certain master-alloy inputs remain import-exposed. Titanium sponge, high-purity nickel and cobalt, and some vacuum-melting consumables are sourced globally; India's domestic titanium-sponge capacity (KMML/DMRL-derived) is limited. MIDHANI's value-add — vacuum induction/arc melting, electroslag remelting, forging and precision casting — is domestic, but the elemental feedstock chain is not fully sovereign.

faq.question: What does MIDHANI make and why is it strategically important?
faq.answer: MIDHANI is a Mini Ratna PSU under the Ministry of Defence that produces superalloys, titanium alloys, special and maraging steels, armour steel, castings, forgings and fasteners. It is the principal — and in several grades the sole — domestic source of high-temperature aero-engine superalloys, maraging steel for strategic missile motor cases, and titanium/special-steel hardware for launch vehicles and warships. It was created in 1973 specifically to break India's dependence on denied Western strategic materials, making it a foundational supplier to DRDO, ISRO, HAL and the armed forces.

faq.question: What were MIDHANI's FY26 financial results?
faq.answer: For FY26 MIDHANI reported record revenue from operations of ₹1,208.63 crore, up 12.52% year-on-year, with Profit After Tax of ₹130.79 crore (up 18.82%) and EPS of ₹6.98. Q4 FY26 revenue was ₹552.75 crore (up 34.63%) with Q4 PAT of ₹77.75 crore. The order book stood at ₹2,290 crore as of 1 April 2026 and the board declared a total dividend of ₹2.10 per share. The company also achieved record titanium-alloy production of about 700 tonnes.

faq.question: What is the significance of the GE Aerospace S400 approval and the ADA MoU?
faq.answer: On 13 August 2026 MIDHANI became the first Indian company to receive GE Aerospace S400 laboratory approval, certifying its chemical, mechanical and metallurgical testing to GE Aerospace standards and positioning it to supply into global aero-engine supply chains. Separately, on 17 February 2025 MIDHANI signed an MoU with the Aeronautical Development Agency to indigenously develop high-strength, high-toughness special steel for India's combat-aircraft programmes — Tejas Mk-2, the Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA) and the Twin Engine Deck-Based Fighter (TEDBF).
